title: [Logging] Cannot use ConsoleAppender for Query and Security Logs
body:
**Version** : 5.3.0-enterprise
**Platform** : irrelevant

It seems the usage of `ConsoleAppender` is filtered out for anything else than `neo4j console` , is there a reason why ? The documentation is highlighting that all the Log4j appenders are supported and there is an example for the ConsoleAppender https://neo4j.com/docs/operations-manual/current/monitoring/logging/#_console_appender

The following `server-logs.xml` produces no logs for query and security logs

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--

    Copyright (c) "Neo4j"
    Neo4j Sweden AB [http://neo4j.com]
    This file is a commercial add-on to Neo4j Enterprise Edition.

-->
<!--
    This is a log4j 2 configuration file.

    It is highly recommended to keep the original "debug.log" as is, to make sure enough data is captured in case
    of errors in a format that neo4j developers can work with.

    All configuration values can be queried with the lookup prefix "config:". You can for example, resolve
    the path to your neo4j home directory with ${config:dbms.directories.neo4j_home}.

    Please consult https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/manual/configuration.html for instructions and
    available configuration options.
-->
<Configuration status="ERROR" monitorInterval="5" packages="org.neo4j.logging.log4j">
    <Appenders>
        <!-- Default debug.log, please keep -->
        <RollingRandomAccessFile name="DebugLog" fileName="${config:server.directories.logs}/debug.log"
                                 filePattern="$${config:server.directories.logs}/debug.log.%02i">
            <Neo4jDebugLogLayout pattern="%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSSZ}{GMT+0} %-5p [%c{1.}] %m%n"/>
            <Policies>
                <SizeBasedTriggeringPolicy size="20 MB"/>
            </Policies>
            <DefaultRolloverStrategy fileIndex="min" max="7"/>
        </RollingRandomAccessFile>
        <Console name="ConsoleAppender" target="SYSTEM_OUT">
            <PatternLayout pattern="%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSSZ}{GMT+0} %-5p %m%n"/>
        </Console>
    </Appenders>

    <Loggers>
        <!-- Log levels. One of DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or OFF -->

        <!-- The debug log is used as the root logger to catch everything -->
        <Root level="INFO">
            <AppenderRef ref="DebugLog"/> <!-- Keep this -->
        </Root>

        <!-- The query log, must be named "QueryLogger" -->
        <Logger name="QueryLogger" level="DEBUG" additivity="true">
            <AppenderRef ref="ConsoleAppender"/>
        </Logger>
        <!-- The security log, must be named "SecurityLogger" -->
        <Logger name="SecurityLogger" level="DEBUG" additivity="true">
            <AppenderRef ref="ConsoleAppender"/>
        </Logger>
    </Loggers>
</Configuration>
```

Reference to the code filtering the console appender https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/5.3/community/logging/src/main/java/org/neo4j/logging/log4j/LogConfig.java#L193

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hello and thanks for reporting!

There is more to it than that filtering, see https://github.com/neo4j/neo4j/blob/5.3/community/neo4j/src/main/java/org/neo4j/server/NeoBootstrapper.java#L145, so all console appenders would be redirected to the log files anyway. I believe the reason behind this was that there is no "natural" console attached to the `neo4j server`(daemonized), since that is highly platform and deployment dependent. In order to keep things as coherent as possible this is what we landed on.

That being said, the complete lack of warnings/log messages/documentation about this is really confusing, and at least that should be improved. I'll see to it!

Just out of curiosity, do you have a particular use case in mind when you want everything to be printed to stdout?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant1 Thanks for the clarification.

I definitely have use cases for stdout, mainly when Neo4j is deployed as a container. Having the ability to have logs produced to the container stdout means that it can leverage all the centralised logging infrastructure.

- We have Neo4j deployed on Kubernetes, we have nothing to do to send logs to loki for container logs
- We have Neo4j deployed on Azure App Services, having logs to Log Analytics is a one click option ( or 2 lines in a template ), while with files based, we have to create a new storage account, create a container and attach the container to the app service.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter alright, that sounds reasonable. The neo4j docker images use `neo4j console` to run, so we have not encountered this limitation before in our testing setup. I'll see if there is a quick workaround until we can get this sorted.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: I'm also interested in a workaround. We are trying to do the same thing for HTTP logs.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter @participant2 A well-tested solution would be to change your containers to use `neo4j console` akin to what neo4j docker and the init.d/systemd services use. Would this work for you?

If you need to emulate the `neo4j server` with console appenders you could spawn a process from the shell, either with `nohup` or the ampersand post-fix(`neo4j console &`) depending on the lifetime of the shell. A `neo4j console` process will react to `neo4j status` and `neo4j stop` the same way the server mode does, so the overall change would be minimal.

This only applies to Linux since Windows services do not have `stdout`/`stdin`/`stderr`. This is one of the reasons we opted for this behavior, to keep things coherent across platforms.

I'll update the documentation for the tarball installation with guidelines on when to use, or when not to use the different modes.

```
    ports:

    environment:
      - NEO4J_dbms_databases_seed__from__uri__providers=URLConnectionSeedProvider,S3SeedProvider

 ```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter The neo4j docker images should use `neo4j console`: https://github.com/neo4j/docker-neo4j/blob/master/docker-image-src/5/docker-entrypoint.sh#L624, so your console appenders should not be removed. Something else must be happening here. 

Could you run with the env `NEO4J_DEBUG=true` and verify that console is indeed used?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter Thanks for all the details, I have reproduced the behavior now. It appears that the `-console-mode` is not properly applied to the `server-logs.xml` and only affects the `user-logs.xml`. This is obviously a bug and not the intended behavior.

I'm working on a fix for it. Sadly I don't have a workaround for you that you can use in the meantime.

Cheers !
